# `silk/time/zones`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Where time zones come from: the `TimeZones` effect, which gives a `Zone` for a name, and the
`LocalZone` effect, which names the zone of this machine.

## When to use

Require `&mut TimeZones` in code that needs the rules of a named zone, such as
`America/Sao_Paulo`. Require `&mut LocalZone` in code that needs to know which zone the
machine is set to. A program provides both with `silk.time.zones_native`, which has one
implementation for each operating system. A test provides [`FixedTimeZones`](#FixedTimeZones) and
[`FixedLocalZone`](#FixedLocalZone), so its result does not depend on the machine.

## Details

The two effects are separate because they come from different places. On some systems the
name of the local zone comes from the operating system, and the rules of all zones come from
data inside the program.

[`TimeZones.zone`](#TimeZones.impl.zone) returns an owned `Zone`. Load a zone one time and keep it; a
`ZonedDateTime` of `silk.time.zoned` borrows it. Every provider gives the zone `UTC` and
fixed offsets such as `+05:30` without any data.

There is no default zone. Code that wants the local time shows `&mut LocalZone` in its
signature.

## Errors

- [`ZoneLookupError`](#ZoneLookupError) from [`TimeZones`](#TimeZones), with a reason: the zone is not known, the name is
  not valid, or the data cannot be read or is damaged.
- [`NoLocalZoneError`](#NoLocalZoneError) from [`LocalZone`](#LocalZone) if the machine does not say which zone it is in.
  The caller decides what to use then; no provider answers `UTC` in silence.

## Examples

### Provide fixed zones in a test

```silk
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.collections.bytes { Bytes }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.time.instant { Instant }
import silk.time.zone { ZoneDataError }
import silk.time.zoned { ZonedDateTime }
import silk.time.zones { FixedLocalZone, FixedTimeZones, LocalZone, NoLocalZoneError, TimeZones, ZoneLookupError }

// The hour that the local clock shows at `at`.
effect fn localHour(at: Instant) -> u8
  ! ZoneLookupError | NoLocalZoneError | OutOfMemoryError
  ? &mut TimeZones | &mut LocalZone | &mut Allocator {
  let name = run LocalZone.name()
  let zone = run TimeZones.zoneBytes(Bytes.asSlice(&name))
  return ZonedDateTime.make(at, &zone).time().hour()
}

effect fn check() -> i32
  ! ZoneDataError | ZoneLookupError | NoLocalZoneError | OutOfMemoryError
  ? &mut Allocator {
  let mut zones = FixedTimeZones.make()
  run zones.addPosixRule("Europe/Rome", "CET-1CEST,M3.5.0,M10.5.0/3")
  let mut here = run FixedLocalZone.make("Europe/Rome")
  let hour = run localHour(Instant.fromUnixSeconds(1795109782))
    |> Effect.provideMut<TimeZones>(&mut zones)
    |> Effect.provideMut<LocalZone>(&mut here)
  if hour != 18 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}

effect fn failed(error: ZoneDataError | ZoneLookupError | NoLocalZoneError | OutOfMemoryError) -> i32 {
  return 2
}

pub effect fn main() -> i32 {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  return run Effect.catchAll(check(), failed) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
}
```

Import as `TimeZones` with `import silk.time.zones { TimeZones }`.

<a id="TimeZones"></a>

## `TimeZones`

```silk
pub service TimeZones
```

The effect that gives the rules of a time zone for its name.

### Details

A name is an identifier of the IANA time zone database, such as `America/Sao_Paulo`. Names
are compared without letter case, and a link such as `Asia/Calcutta` is accepted. The zone
has the name as the provider spells it, so `america/sao_paulo` gives a zone named
`America/Sao_Paulo`, and a link keeps its own name. `UTC` and an offset such as `+05:30` or
`-03` give a zone with that fixed offset from every provider.

A provider is the choice of where the rules come from: the files of the operating system
(`OsTimeZones` of `silk.time.zones_native`), or zones that the program supplies
([`FixedTimeZones`](#FixedTimeZones)).

<a id="TimeZones.zoneBytes"></a>

### Operation `zoneBytes`

```silk
effect fn zoneBytes(
    name: &[u8]
  ) -> Zone ! ZoneLookupError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut TimeZones | &mut Allocator
```

Returns the zone named by the bytes `name`.

#### Errors

- [`ZoneLookupError`](#ZoneLookupError) with the reason `UnknownZone` if the provider has no such zone,
  `InvalidName` if `name` cannot be a zone name, `Unreadable` if the provider cannot read
  its data, or `InvalidData` if the data of the zone is damaged.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the zone.

<a id="TimeZones.names"></a>

### Operation `names`

```silk
effect fn names() -> List<Bytes> ! ZoneLookupError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut TimeZones | &mut Allocator
```

Returns copies of the names of all zones of the provider, sorted by their bytes. `UTC` and
the fixed offsets are not in the list.

#### Errors

- [`ZoneLookupError`](#ZoneLookupError) with the reason `Unreadable` if the provider cannot list its zones.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the copies.

<a id="TimeZones.version"></a>

### Operation `version`

```silk
effect fn version() -> Bytes ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut TimeZones | &mut Allocator
```

Returns the version of the time zone database that the provider uses, such as `2026b`, or
empty bytes if the provider does not know it.

#### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the copy.

### Associated function `zone`

```silk
pub effect fn zone(
    name: string
  ) -> Zone ! ZoneLookupError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut TimeZones | &mut Allocator
```

Returns the zone named `name`, such as `America/Sao_Paulo`.

#### Errors

- [`ZoneLookupError`](#ZoneLookupError) and `OutOfMemoryError`, as for [`TimeZones.zoneBytes`](#TimeZones.zoneBytes).

<a id="TimeZones.impl.fixedZone"></a>

### Associated function `fixedZone`

```silk
pub fn fixedZone(name: &[u8]) -> Option<Zone>
```

Returns the zone for a name that needs no data: `UTC` in any letter case, or an offset
such as `+05:30`, `-0300`, or `+01`. Returns `None` for other names. Providers call it
first.

<a id="TimeZones.impl.isValidName"></a>

### Associated function `isValidName`

```silk
pub fn isValidName(name: &[u8]) -> bool
```

Returns `true` if `name` has the form of a zone name: 1 to 255 bytes of ASCII letters,
digits, `/`, `_`, `-`, `+`, and `.`, in parts separated by `/`, where no part is empty, `.`,
or `..`.

#### When to use

A provider that turns a name into a file path calls it first, so that a name cannot leave
the directory of the zones.

<a id="TimeZones.impl.sameName"></a>

### Associated function `sameName`

```silk
pub fn sameName(left: &[u8], right: &[u8]) -> bool
```

Returns `true` if `left` and `right` are the same zone name, without letter case.

<a id="TimeZones.impl.lookupFailure"></a>

### Associated function `lookupFailure`

```silk
pub fn lookupFailure(reason: ZoneLookupReason) -> ZoneLookupError
```

Returns a [`ZoneLookupError`](#ZoneLookupError) with the reason `reason`. Providers use it.

<a id="LocalZone"></a>

## `LocalZone`

```silk
pub service LocalZone
```

The effect that names the time zone of this machine.

### Details

The answer is a zone name to give to [`TimeZones.zoneBytes`](#TimeZones.zoneBytes), such as `America/Sao_Paulo`. It
is read at each call, so a program sees a change of the setting.

<a id="LocalZone.name"></a>

### Operation `name`

```silk
effect fn name() -> Bytes ! NoLocalZoneError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut LocalZone | &mut Allocator
```

Returns a copy of the name of the zone that this machine is set to.

#### Errors

- [`NoLocalZoneError`](#NoLocalZoneError) if the machine does not say which zone it is in.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the copy.

<a id="FixedTimeZones"></a>

## `FixedTimeZones`

```silk
pub struct FixedTimeZones
```

A `TimeZones` provider with the zones that the program gives it, for tests and for programs
that carry their own zone data.

### Details

Add each zone with [`FixedTimeZones.addTzif`](#FixedTimeZones.impl.addTzif) or [`FixedTimeZones.addPosixRule`](#FixedTimeZones.impl.addPosixRule). The
provider keeps a copy of the data and makes the zone at each lookup. A name that is added
again replaces the earlier one.

<a id="FixedTimeZones.impl.addTzif"></a>

### Method `addTzif`

```silk
pub effect fn addTzif(self: &mut Self, name: string, data: &[u8]) -> ()
    ! ZoneDataError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Adds the zone `name` with the bytes of a TZif file, the format of the files under
`/usr/share/zoneinfo`.

#### Errors

- `ZoneDataError` if `data` is not a valid TZif file.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the copy.

<a id="FixedTimeZones.impl.addPosixRule"></a>

### Method `addPosixRule`

```silk
pub effect fn addPosixRule(self: &mut Self, name: string, rule: string) -> ()
    ! ZoneDataError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Adds the zone `name` with a POSIX `TZ` rule such as `CET-1CEST,M3.5.0,M10.5.0/3`. See
`Zone.fromPosixRule` for the form of a rule.

#### Errors

- `ZoneDataError` if `rule` is not a valid rule.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the copy.
